to lie (lying down) / to be located
lie → liegen. Things lying flat: the book liegt on the table.
The book is (lying) on the table.
Old English 'hight' (named), as in 'a knight hight Lancelot'. Wie heißt du? = What are you called?
believe → glauben: the 'lieve' in believe is the 'lauben'. Ich glaube dir = I believe you.
Related to 'token' and 'teach' (to show). Picture a pointer: zeig mal! = show me!
Führer just means leader, guide. Führerschein = driving licence (a 'leading' licence). Führen = to lead.
speak → sprechen (k becomes ch, plus an extra r).
Hidden in English 'frame a question'? Better: Old English 'fricgan' (ask). Picture a frog that asks endless questions: frag, frag, frag!
Sales spiel = a speech you play out. Spielen = to play (games, sports, music). Spiel = game.
Picture an arbour (garden arch) you work all day to build: Arbeit = work. 'Arbeit macht' you tired.
You NEED to fix your BROKEN brow: brauchen. Ich brauche Hilfe = I need help.
follow → folgen. Folg mir! = Follow me!
Like 'under-stand': ver + stehen (stand). Ich verstehe = I understand.
to set, put / to sit down (sich setzen)
set → setzen. Setz dich! = Sit down (set yourself)!
Classic trap: NOT 'become'. Ich bekomme ein Geschenk = I GET a present. 'Ich bekomme ein Steak' does not turn you into beef!
tell / tale → erzählen (t becomes z). Telling a tale.
ver + suchen (seek): to seek a way, to attempt. Versuch = attempt.
scribe / scribble → schreiben. A scribe writes.
leap / lope → laufen. The film läuft = it's running (showing).
He is sitting in the garden.
On German doors: ZIEHEN = pull, DRÜCKEN = push. Related to English 'tug' and 'tow'.
shine → scheinen. Die Sonne scheint = the sun is shining.
ge + hören (hear): what belongs to you 'hears' you, obeys you. Das gehört mir = that's mine.
ent (start) + stehen (stand): something that stands up out of nowhere, arises.
er + halten (hold): to get hold of what arrived. More formal than bekommen.
Treff = a meeting point. Picture two people bumping into each other: they treffen, they meet (and hit) each other.
seek → suchen (k becomes ch). Hide and seek!
lay → legen. Flat things are laid: legen. Upright things are stood: stellen.
Put the book on the table.
handle → handeln. Es handelt sich um = it's about.
Related to 'drag' (d becomes t). You carry and drag your stuff; you also wear (carry) clothes.
shape → schaffen: to shape something, to get it done. Wir schaffen das! = We can do it!
Related to 'lecture' and 'legend' (Latin legere, to read). Ich lese = I read.
lose / forlorn → verlieren. Forlorn = lost and hopeless, same root.
er + kennen (know): to know again, recognise. Kennen ≈ 'ken' (knowledge).
ent (un-) + wickeln (wrap) = un-wrap, exactly like English de-velop (un-wrap).
Picture a talk show host with a RED face: he never stops talking. Wir müssen reden = We need to talk.
aus (out) + sehen (see) = how you look from the outside. Du siehst müde aus = You look tired.
build → bilden. Bildung = education, building a person. Bildungsroman!
an (on) + fangen (catch, like 'fang'): you catch onto something and start. More casual than beginnen.
I expect a lot from you.
'Where do you live?' 'Over YON (wohn) hill!' Wohnung = flat, apartment.
help → helfen (p becomes f). Hilfe! = Help!
shut / slot → schließen. Schloss = lock (and castle!), Schlüssel = key.
er + inner: to bring back inside. Sich erinnern = to remember.
study → studieren. For school learning use lernen.
fail → fehlen. Du fehlst mir = I miss you (you are missing to me).
Related to Deutsch (the 'people's' language): bedeuten = to make plain to the people, to mean.
eat → essen (t becomes ss). Ich esse = I eat.
What do you like to eat?
Related to 'cheap' (old word for trade). Picture a cow you buy at market: kaufen. Kaufhaus = department store.
be + zahlen (count, like 'tally' / 'tell' money). You pay by counting out money.
fare / farewell → fahren. Gute Fahrt = have a good trip (fare well!).
open → öffnen (p becomes f). Offen = open.
A dog barks 'RUFF!' to call you. Ruf mich an! = Call me (on the phone)!
answer and Antwort share a root: an(d) + word = a word back. Wort = word.
love / lief ('I'd as lief') → lieben. Ich liebe dich = I love you.
may / might → mögen. Ich mag Pizza = I like pizza. (It's also 'may' in ich möchte, I'd like.)
Darf ich? = May I? Asking permission. Können is ability, dürfen is permission.
ken (as in 'beyond my ken') / know → kennen. For people and places; facts use wissen.
do → tun (d becomes t). Es tut mir leid = I'm sorry.
starve → sterben. Starving used to mean dying.
Das gefällt mir = that pleases me, I like it (the thing is the subject, like Spanish 'me gusta').
pass → passieren: what passes, happens. Was ist passiert? = What happened?
ver + kaufen (buy) = the opposite of buying: selling.
cook → kochen (k becomes ch). Koch = cook, chef.
laugh → lachen. The gh in laugh used to sound just like this ch.
whine → weinen. A whining baby cries.
stall / install → stellen: to make something stand. Eine Frage stellen = to ask a question.
haul → holen. You haul it over. Ich hole dich ab = I'll pick you up.
Sending a CHICKEN by post: schicken. Schick mir... = send me...
Zahl = number, like 'tally'. Zahlen, bitte! = The bill, please!
other → ändern: to make other, alter.
Hidden in 'neighbour' (neigh-bour = near dweller). Bauhaus = building house. Bauer = farmer.
to choose / to vote / to dial
Related to 'will' (choice). Wahl = election. You dial (wählen) a number too.
Teil = part, related to 'deal' (a share of cards). Wir teilen = we share.
be + suchen (seek): to go and seek someone out.
bid (as in 'do as I bid') → bitten. Bitte = please.
Related to 'fair' (festival) and Latin feria. Feierabend = time off after work.
